column2: One should give according to ability and have it said in the divine and ancestral rites: "May the Vishvedevas be pleased"; one should dismiss at the Vaja.
Having followed with "Amavajasya" and circumambulated the Brahmins, one should enter the house; one should do so on the new moon month after month.
I shall tell the Ekoddishta: one should perform the ancestral rite as before; one purifier, one half-arghya, one pinda should be given;
no invocation or fire-offering, and no Vishvedevas here. At the question of satisfaction the Brahmin should say "Well-tasted," "Pleasant."
Let it stand near at the imperishable; at dismissal "Take delight"; others say "We are delighted"; the rest as before.
I shall tell the Sapindikarana, at the end of the year or in the middle: for the fathers three vessels, and one vessel for the departed;
four with purifiers, with sesame and flowers, joined with scented water; having filled, one sprinkles.
One should pour the ghost's vessel into the ancestors' vessels with the verse "Ye samanah"; as before giving pinda and the rest, the ghosts attain ancestor-hood.
Now I shall tell the Abhyudayika ancestral rite — all as before, one should recite excluding the ancestral mantras; in the forenoon with circumambulation;
the attendances with straight kusha, sesame and barley here; at the question of satisfaction the Brahmin should say "Accomplished, well accomplished."
Pindas with curds, rice, jujube and the like; "I shall invoke the Nandimukha ancestors" — one should ask; and at the imperishable "May they be pleased."
The Nandimukha ancestors, I shall have it said, then one asks: "Let the Nandimukha hosts of ancestors be pleased," one should say.
The Nandimukha ancestors, his father, great-grandfather; the maternal grandfather, maternal great-grandfather, old maternal great-grandfather;
one should not use the word svadha; one should feed an even number of Brahmins. I shall tell the satisfaction of the ancestors: with village herbs a month,
likewise with forest roots, tubers and fruits a month; with fish two months, with deer three, with birds,
four with Raurava deer, five and six with goat; with tortoise seven, eight; with boar nine,
with mutton ten, with buffalo, spotted deer and jackals; a year with cow's milk or pudding;
with the flesh of the Vardhrinasa bird, satisfaction for twelve years; rhinoceros flesh, kalashaka, red goat, honey,
great shalka fish in the rains; the Magha ancestral rite is imperishable. The Mantra-reciter, Agnihotrin, Shakha-reciter, knower of the six limbs,
Trinachiketa, Trimadhu, reciter of Dharmadrona, Trisuparna, knower of Jyeshtha Saman — these purify a row.
I shall tell the desire-rite: on pratipada much wealth; on dvitiya women supreme; on chaturthi giver of dharma and desire;
on panchami one desiring sons; on shashthi a sharer of excellence; and a farmer on saptami; on ashtami gainer of wealth;
on navami one-hoofed animals; on dashami cattle herds; on ekadashi retinue; on dvadashi wealth and grain;
on trayodashi eminence among kin; on chaturdashi, for those dead by weapon; the ancestral rite for all is declared on the new moon.
Seven hunters in Dasharna forest, deer on Kalanjara mountain, chakravaka birds on Sharadvipa, swans on Lake Manasa —
they too were born at Kurukshetra as Brahmins, masters of the Veda; set out on a long road; you sink for them.
When recited at the ancestral rite and the like, the ancestral rite becomes full, giving Brahma's world. A son or other should perform the ancestral rite for a father while his father is living —
for his father's father, and his father's father; while the great-grandfather lives, for the father's grandfather, and for the other great-grandfather;
thus for the mother and others, and likewise for the maternal grandfather and others. Whoever recites the ritual of the ancestral rite obtains the fruit of the performer.
At a sacred place, at the beginning of an age, at the beginning of a Manu-period, a given ancestral rite is imperishable. The bright ninth of Ashvina, the twelfth in Kartika,
the third of Magha and likewise of Bhadrapada, the new moon of Phalguna, and the eleventh of Pausha,
the tenth of Ashadha, the seventh of the month of Magha, the dark eighth in Shravana, and the full moon in Ashadha,
the full moons of Kartika and Phalguna likewise, the bright fifteenth of Jyeshtha; the Manus beginning with Svayambhuva, of them the first are imperishable.
Gaya, Prayaga, Ganga, Kurukshetra and Narmada, Shriparvata, Prabhasa, Shalagrama, Varanasi,
Godavari — the ancestral rite at these, and at Strishothama and others.
Nagadvipa, then Saumya, Gandharva, then Varuna; this ninth among them is an island surrounded by the sea.
This island is thousands of yojanas from south to north. Bharata has nine divisions; in the central division, then from the east,
Kiratas and Yavanas, and Brahmins and the rest in the middle. The rivers from the Vedasmriti and Pariyatra,
from Vindhya Narmada and others; from Sahya Tapi and Payoshni; Godavari, Bhimarathi, Krishnaveni and others;
from Malaya the Kritamala and others; from Mahendra the Trisama and others; Kumara and others from Shuktimat; from Himalaya the Chandrabhaga;
in the west stand Kuru, Panchala, the Middle Country and the rest.
Surrounded by sugarcane-juice ocean by measure, twice as large is Shalmali; Vapushmat's seven sons became lords of Shalmali.
Shveta, Harita, Jimuta, Lohita in order, Vaidyuta, Manasa and Suprabha were named the regions.
Twice as large, surrounded by a sea of liquor likewise twice; Kumuda, Anala, and third Valahaka,
Drona, Kanka, then Mahisha, Kakudman — seven rivers; Kapila, Aruna, Pita, Krishna — the Brahmins and others.
They worshipped the form of Vayu; this is surrounded by the liquor sea. Jyotishmat's sons were lords of Kusha: Udbhija, Dhenuman,
Dvairatha, Lamvana, Dhairya, Kapila and Prabhakara; the Brahmins and others with Dadhimukhya worship the form of Brahma.
Vidruma, Hemashaila, Dyutiman, Pushpavan; Kusheshaya, Hari, Shaila, and for rains the Mandara mountain.
This is surrounded by a ghee ocean and by Krauncha island; the lords of Krauncha are Dyutimat's sons, regions named for them:
Kushala, Manonuga, Ushna, Pradhana, Andhakaraka, Muni and Dundubhi — seven and seven mountains and rivers.
Krauncha, Vamana, and third Andhakaraka, Devavrit, Pundarika and Dundubhi, each twice the other.
The islands, and the mountains in the islands, as the islands so those; the Brahmins and others worship Hari at Pushkara, Pushkala and Dhanya sacred places;
Krauncha island is surrounded by a curd-whey ocean; surrounded by Shaka island, whose lords of Shaka are the sons of Havya:
Jalada and Kumara, Sukumara, Manivaka, Kushottara, Modaki, Druma — regions named for them.
Udaya, Jaladhara, Raivata, Shyamaka, Kodraka, Ambikeya, Ramya, Keshari — seven rivers.
The Magas, Magadhas, Manasyas and Mandagas, twice-born, worship the form of the Sun; Shaka is surrounded by the milk ocean.
Surrounded by Pushkara, there are two sons of Savana: Masavita and Dhataki, two regions marked with names.
One mountain called Manasa is here in the middle, ring-shaped; thousands of yojanas in breadth and height equal;
life ten thousand years; Brahma is worshipped here by the gods. Surrounded by the sweet-water sea by measure of the island;
in the oceans no deficiency or excess of water arises. At the rising and setting of the moon, in the bright and dark fortnights,
five hundred and ten fingers, the increase and decrease of the oceans' waters is seen, O great sage.
Sweet-watered, of many qualities, a golden land free of creatures; then the Lokaloka mountain, extending ten thousand yojanas.
Lokaloka is covered with darkness; then the shell of the egg; the earth with the egg-shell is fifty crores in extent.
The empty fifteenth and Tuesday, having worshipped Sarasvati, Hari and Shri; in the six months beginning with Magha the girdle-tying is auspicious;
the tonsure and the like are not praised in Shravana and others; when Jupiter and Venus have set and the moon is waned,
one should declare death or dullness for an initiated Brahmin. At a shaving star on an auspicious day the return home is desired;
in auspicious lunar mansions, with the ascendant, joined with and aspected by benefics; in Ashvini, Magha, Chitra, Svati, Bharani and Uttara,
Punarvasu and Pushya, the study of archery is praised. In Bharani, Ardra, Magha, Ashlesha, and the fire and Bhaga stars,
one wishing to live should not put on a new garment. On Thursday, Friday and Wednesday, cloth at marriage and the like, not stars;
in Revati, Ashvini, Dhanishtha and the five beginning with Hasta, wearing conch, coral and jewels is praised.
In Bharani, Ashlesha, Dhanishtha, the three Purvas, and Shatabhisha, goods bought bring loss, sold bring gain;
in Ashvini, Svati, Chitra, Revati, Shatabhisha, Shravana, goods bought bring gain, sold bring loss.
Bharani, the three Purvas, Ardra, Ashlesha, Magha, Svati, Krittika, Jyeshtha and Vishakha: the owner does not obtain.
Wealth given, lent, or deposited — in Uttara, Shravana, Jyeshtha, one should do a king's coronation.
Chaitra, Jyeshtha, Bhadra, Ashvina, Pausha and Magha being left, in the remaining months a house is auspicious;
Ashvini, Rohini, Mula, the three Uttaras, Mrigashira, Svati, Hasta and Anuradha are praised at the start of building a house;
excluding Sunday and Tuesday, likewise for a well and a temple. When Jupiter is in Leo, in Guru-Aditya conjunction, in the intercalary month,
when Venus is young, old or set, one should avoid house-work. Fire, fear, disease, king's oppression, loss of wealth
come when collecting grass and wood in the five Shravana. One should enter a house in Dhanishtha, Uttara and Shatabhisha.
In building a boat: the second, third, fifth, seventh and thirteenth; seeing a king: Dhanishtha, Hasta, Revati and Ashvini;
the three Purvas, Dhanishtha, Ardra, Krittika, Mrigashira and Vishakha; Ashlesha and Ashvini — success of a journey with wealth.
In the three Uttaras, Rohini, Sinivali and chaturdashi; Shravana, Hasta, Chitra and Vishnu's;
one should not undertake a cattle-pen journey nor cause entry. In Anila, Uttara, Rohini, Mrigashira, Mula and Punarvasu,
in Pushya, Shravana and Hasta one should do agriculture; in Punarvasu, Uttara, Svati, Bhaga, Mula, Indra's and Varuna's,
on Thursday or Friday, or on Monday and Sunday; and in Taurus, Virgo and Gemini ascendants it should be done.
